notes: Line-by-line check. NHS excerpts support: weight gain, increased appetite, sleep problems, indigestion, headaches and mood changes as common effects; taking it with food and in the morning; serious effects more likely at high dose or beyond 2 weeks (infection, high blood sugar, Cushing's, adrenal problems, mood); long-term bone thinning, diabetes, eye problems, high blood pressure, muscle weakness, cataracts; blue steroid card for >3 weeks or high dose and red emergency card; no sudden stopping after >3 weeks; live vaccines avoided; chickenpox/shingles exposure reported; check before OTC ibuprofen or herbal remedies. No new dose figure added (3-4 week card threshold and 3-week taper threshold predate the patch; the NHS '40 mg' figure was not imported). Liquorice interaction and diabetes-treatment adjustment are stated as NHS/clinician-mediated, not as instructions. Eye-drop and rectal uses are MedlinePlus product facts. No protected field changed.
